one_liner: Pure-Rust, ZeroMQ wire-compatible (ZMTP 3.x) async messaging library; about 3x lower REQ/REP latency than libzmq.
what_it_does: Monocoque reimplements the ZeroMQ wire protocol (ZMTP 3.x) from scratch in Rust. Its sockets talk to libzmq 4.1+ peers on the wire, but it does not wrap or reproduce libzmq's C API. It provides the 11 classic socket types (REQ/REP, DEALER/ROUTER, PUB/SUB, XPUB/XSUB, PUSH/PULL, PAIR) plus a StreamSocket, over TCP, IPC (Unix sockets) and an in-process channel bridge, with NULL, PLAIN, CURVE and ZAP security. The API is async-only: no blocking send/recv, no context object, no zmq_poll, and multipart messages are sent and received as a whole Vec<Bytes>. It runs on compio/io_uring by default, or on tokio or smol, chosen by a compile-time feature.
how_it_is_fast: The main latency lever is that there is no background I/O thread. send() and recv() do the I/O inline on the caller's single-threaded runtime (thread-per-core, and sockets are !Send). libzmq instead passes every message through a lock-free queue to a separate I/O thread. The arena data backs this up: the epoll-based tokio backend matches or beats the io_uring default on REQ/REP (IPC 16 B: 9.36 vs 13.08 us p50), so the win comes from removing the thread hop, not from io_uring. For bulk traffic it uses refcounted Bytes (PUB fan-out clones references and never copies payloads), a reused 64 KiB read slab, allocation-free recv_into, writev for bodies of 32 KB and up, and opt-in write coalescing that packs many small frames into one 64 KB write. The arena's throughput cells turn coalescing on; its REQ/REP cells do not.
when_to_use: Rust services on Linux that must talk to existing libzmq/pyzmq peers and want lower request/reply latency: in the arena run, REQ/REP p50 was about 13-22 us against 40-61 us for libzmq across 16 B-16 KiB payloads.
Same-host request/reply over IPC: with the tokio backend, p50 was 9.36-9.70 us at 16 B-1 KiB against 40.17-42.16 us for libzmq.

Small-message PUSH/PULL pipelines where you can call flush() at batch boundaries: coalesced PUSH/PULL reached 13.3 M msg/s at 64 B over IPC against 2.84 M msg/s for libzmq, and 7.6 M vs 3.1 M over TCP.
PUB/SUB fan-out to many subscribers: at 32 subscribers it delivered 1.7x-4.5x libzmq's message rate, with lower peak RSS (35 MB vs 162 MB at 16 KiB).
Async Rust codebases already on tokio or smol: pick the matching backend feature and run the sockets on a current-thread runtime.
when_not_to_use: Non-Rust callers, or code that depends on libzmq's C ABI, blocking send/recv, zmq_poll or libzmq's many language bindings. This is an async Rust library only.

Deployments that need transports or features beyond TCP/IPC: PGM/EPGM, TIPC, draft sockets and GSSAPI are listed as skipped in the CHANGELOG, and inproc is a channel bridge that the migration guide says is not the same as libzmq inproc.

Security-critical CURVE setups that need a track record. Before 0.4.0 (2026-07-31) the CURVE message cipher was not the real CurveZMQ construction, so encrypted interop with libzmq never worked. That same release also closed several pre-auth DoS holes (slow-loris recv timeout, unbounded handshake, unbounded multipart).

Fan-in of many tiny messages from many producers: at 4-peer fan-in with 16 B messages, the default compio backend reached only 0.94x libzmq's rate. At 1 KiB its peak RSS was 85.6 MB against 38.5 MB for libzmq.

Teams that need a mature dependency. The crate was first published on 2026-06-22 and has 312 total downloads and 46 stars. It is essentially single-maintainer (49 of 50 issues were filed by the author) and pre-1.0, with breaking changes in 0.3.0 and 0.4.0.

integration.form: crate (monocoque-rs; library name `monocoque`; the ZeroMQ API sits behind the opt-in `zmq` feature)
integration.dependencies: No libzmq or C library. Requires exactly one runtime: compio 0.19 (default, io_uring), tokio or smol. Also pulls bytes, compio-io/compio-buf, tracing and flume, plus dashmap, parking_lot, hashbrown, smallvec, socket2 and zeroize in the core crate. The workspace declares RustCrypto x25519-dalek, crypto_box, chacha20poly1305 and sha2 for PLAIN/CURVE.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.95 (edition 2024) for every backend, as checked in CI. The manifest notes that the tokio/smol backends can compile as far back as 1.93.
integration.platforms: Linux first: the io_uring default needs kernel 5.11+ for the full benefit and falls back to thread-pool I/O on older kernels. The docs offer the tokio/smol backends for macOS, Windows and older kernels, but CI runs only on ubuntu-latest. IPC is Unix-only.
integration.thread_safety: Sockets are !Send on every backend. Run one single-threaded runtime per thread (compio runtime, current-thread tokio in a LocalSet, or smol LocalExecutor) and scale by running one runtime per core. The worker-pool PubSocket shards fan-out writes across its own worker threads.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — wire-compatible with libzmq 4.1+ peers (ZMTP 3.x with NULL/PLAIN/CURVE), so it can replace one side of an existing ZeroMQ deployment. It is not an API or ABI replacement: it is async Rust only, has no context and no zmq_poll (futures::select! instead), handles multipart messages as a single Vec<Bytes>, and sets options through a SocketOptions builder.

gotchas: Write coalescing is off by default, so each eager send() is one syscall (about 0.44-0.52 M msg/s at 64 B in the project's local bench). Turning coalescing on makes you own flush(): in request/reply, forgetting flush() before recv() deadlocks, and messages still in the buffer are lost if the process crashes.

Cancelling a send future mid-write (a timeout, or a losing select! branch) poisons the socket, and later I/O fails with BrokenPipe, 'reconnect required'. This matters because the migration guide suggests futures::select! as the replacement for zmq_poll.

On the tokio backend, the worker-pool PubSocket's writes depend on the runtime that accepted the subscriber. A short-lived publisher that lets that runtime shut down right after sending can drop the tail of its broadcast.

Benchmark caveat: the run kept the default cgroup cpuset 0-3. The arena's own README says that setting is only correct on four distinct physical performance cores. The i5-13400 is a hybrid SMT part, and libzmq's extra I/O thread per process competes for those four logical CPUs, so the gap may be different on other hardware.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Monocoque over TCPSHM when the other side must stay a stock ZeroMQ peer: TCPSHM uses its own protocol and wins on raw same-host RTT, especially in shared-memory mode. Pick it over NanoMsg when you need ZMTP wire compatibility and CURVE rather than nanomsg's own SP protocols.
verified_claims_summary: In zmq-arena's 2026-08-26 run on a bare-metal i5-13400 (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8, turbo off), monocoque 0.4.1 (rustc 1.96, fat LTO, x86-64-v3) had REQ/REP p50 round trips 2.69x-3.12x lower than Ubuntu's libzmq 4.3.5 package. libzmq was driven from an -O3 C++ wrapper with one I/O thread; example cells are 13.79 vs 42.16 us over IPC at 1 KiB and 15.48 vs 42.99 us over TCP at 1 KiB. Monocoque's author wrote the harness and published both run files, and no third party has reproduced them.
status_note: Actively maintained (0.4.2 released 2026-09-22 after roughly monthly releases since June 2026) and MIT-licensed, but it is pre-1.0, single-maintainer and lightly used, so pin the version and expect API breaks between minor releases.
